summary: Adds a `stash auth login` command (device-code flow + device binding via the new native dependency @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2), makes authentication the mandatory first step of `stash init`, removes the CS_* credential guidance from init's next steps and from the README (which now says no env vars are needed for local development), and pins/downgrades several runtime dependencies of the published @cipherstash/stack package (evlog 1.11.0 -> 1.9.0, @byteslice/result 0.2.2 -> 0.2.0). No encryption, payload or SQL paths change. The main risks are in the published CLI: it now statically loads an unseen native package at startup and none of the CLI is built or exercised by CI; `stash init` can no longer complete without interactive network auth; and the new documentation contradicts code that still requires CS_* env vars (`stash secrets`, LockContext). Library runtime risk is limited to the dependency downgrades, which CI tests ran against.

behaviour_changes.description: New CLI subcommand `stash auth login`: prompts for a region from a hard-coded list, runs a device-code flow via @cipherstash/auth (opens a browser, polls for a token saved by the library to ~/.cipherstash/auth.json), then binds the device to the default keyset; bind failure exits with status 1.

`stash init` (and `stash init --supabase`) now runs an authentication step first; it is unconditional, with no skip flag and no check for existing credentials, so init cannot reach connection selection, schema generation or forge install without a successful interactive login and device bind.
Running auth (directly or via init) writes a token to the user's home directory and binds the device to the workspace's default keyset on the CipherStash service. Re-running init repeats both.

The CLI entry statically imports the auth command, so every `stash` invocation (including --help and secrets) now loads @cipherstash/auth, a native Node-API package with per-platform optional binaries, via a default import.

Init next steps no longer tell users to create an account and set CS_WORKSPACE_CRN/CS_CLIENT_ID/CS_CLIENT_KEY/CS_CLIENT_ACCESS_KEY; README says no env vars are needed for local development and that the SDK and CLI use ~/.cipherstash/auth.json; the README TOML config section and the note that the CLI reads CS_* vars are removed.

Published package dependencies changed from caret ranges to exact pins; lockfile resolution for @cipherstash/stack moves evlog 1.11.0 -> 1.9.0 and @byteslice/result 0.2.2 -> 0.2.0 (downgrades), and adds @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2.

failure_scenarios.title: Published stash CLI fails at startup for every command because @cipherstash/auth does not load
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user installs the released package and runs any `stash` command, on a platform or packaging where @cipherstash/auth's default export or native binary does not resolve as the bundled ESM bin expects.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: stash.ts statically imports commands/auth/index.js (stash.ts:7), which imports login.ts, which does `import auth from '@cipherstash/auth'` and destructures beginDeviceCodeFlow/bindClientDevice at module load (login.ts:2-3). A load or interop error is thrown before main() runs, so it is not caught by main().catch. The bin is a separate tsup build (tsup.config.ts:26-41) that CI does not build or run: `pnpm run test` runs vitest with turbo dependsOn ^build only, and no test file covers src/bin.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Every stash command, including `stash secrets` and `--help`, crashes for affected users of that published version; recovery requires a new npm release.

existing_verification.description: CI 'Run Tests' passed, but it runs vitest for packages and does not build or execute the stash bin.

missing_verification: Build the package and run `node dist/bin/stash.js --help` and `stash auth --help` from a packed tarball on the supported platforms (linux gnu/musl, darwin, windows).
Confirm @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2 exposes a CommonJS module.exports (default import) with beginDeviceCodeFlow and bindClientDevice.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Lazy-load @cipherstash/auth inside the auth command/step (dynamic import) so other commands do not depend on it, and add a CLI smoke test of the built bin to CI.

failure_scenarios.title: stash init cannot complete without interactive network login and device binding
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs `stash init` offline, behind a proxy, in a non-interactive shell, in an unlisted region, or without wanting a device bound (e.g. already holding CS_* machine credentials), or the device code expires / binding fails.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: authenticateStep is unconditionally first in STEPS (init/index.ts:16-22) and calls selectRegion, login and bindDevice (authenticate.ts:7-11). login() has no error handling around beginDeviceCodeFlow/pollForToken (login.ts:31-52), so failures propagate to main() as 'Fatal error'; bindDevice calls process.exit(1) on failure (login.ts:54-65). Neither is a CancelledError, so init aborts before any scaffolding. There is no flag to skip or detect an existing token.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Onboarding command that previously worked offline is blocked for these users; re-running init re-authenticates and re-binds the device each time. Loud and recoverable, but affects the documented first step of the quick start.
missing_verification: No tests for the init flow or authenticate step (no test file maps to src/bin).
Manual check of init behaviour when auth fails or when already authenticated.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Skip the step when a valid token or CS_* credentials already exist, add a `--skip-auth` flag, and convert auth failures into a clear message with a retry or continue option.

failure_scenarios.title: New docs and init next steps say no env vars are needed, but stash secrets and LockContext still require CS_* credentials
failure_scenarios.trigger: A new user follows the updated README / init next steps (auth login only, no CS_* vars, no cipherstash.toml) and runs `stash secrets ...` or constructs a LockContext; possibly also Encryption() if protect-ffi 0.21.0 does not read ~/.cipherstash/auth.json.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: README now states 'No environment variables or credentials are needed for local development ... the SDK and CLI will use the token saved to ~/.cipherstash/auth.json' (README.md:497, 451) and init next steps drop the CS_* instructions (base.ts:14). At head, secrets getConfig still exits with 'Missing required environment variables' when CS_WORKSPACE_CRN/CS_CLIENT_ID/CS_CLIENT_KEY are unset (helpers.ts:33-57), and LockContext calls loadWorkSpaceId which throws without CS_WORKSPACE_CRN or cipherstash.toml (identity/index.ts:62, utils/config/index.ts:66-70). Encryption delegates credential fallback to protect-ffi newClient (encryption/index.ts:79-90), which this change does not touch; whether it reads auth.json is unknown.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Documented local-development path fails with credential errors for the secrets CLI and identity-bound encryption, and the guidance on how to fix it (CS_* vars, TOML) has been removed from the README and init output.
missing_verification: End-to-end check that Encryption() initialises with only ~/.cipherstash/auth.json present and no CS_* vars.
Check of `stash secrets` and LockContext under the same conditions.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Either make secrets/identity read the auth token, or scope the README claim to what works (e.g. Encryption only) and keep the CS_* guidance for secrets and lock contexts.

failure_scenarios.title: Downgraded and exact-pinned runtime dependencies change library behaviour for consumers
failure_scenarios.trigger: Consumers install the new @cipherstash/stack release and the library logger or Result helpers rely on behaviour present only in evlog 1.11 / @byteslice/result 0.2.2.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: package.json pins evlog 1.9.0 and @byteslice/result 0.2.0 (package.json:209-212); the lockfile moves stack from evlog 1.11.0 and @byteslice/result 0.2.2 to the older versions. The logger uses evlog initLogger/createRequestLogger (utils/logger/index.ts:1). Exact pins also prevent deduplication with consumers' own versions.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Possible logging differences or duplicate installs for consumers; no data or encryption effect identified.

evidence.claim: authCommand 'login' runs selectRegion, login and bindDevice; unknown subcommands exit 1.
Default-imports @cipherstash/auth and destructures beginDeviceCodeFlow/bindClientDevice at module load; login has no try/catch; bindDevice calls process.exit(1) on failure; regions are hard-coded.
authenticateStep is first in STEPS; only CancelledError is handled, other errors are rethrown.
Step unconditionally calls selectRegion, login, bindDevice with no skip or existing-credential check.
CLI entry statically imports authCommand alongside init and secrets commands.
Runtime dependencies now exact-pinned and include @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2.
Next steps no longer include account creation or CS_* env var instructions (same change in supabase.ts).
README states no env vars are needed for local development and that SDK and CLI use ~/.cipherstash/auth.json; TOML section removed.
stash secrets getConfig still reads only CS_* env vars and exits 1 if missing.
loadWorkSpaceId throws without CS_WORKSPACE_CRN or cipherstash.toml; used by LockContext (identity/index.ts:62).
Encryption client passes credentials to protect-ffi newClient, which handles env fallback internally; auth.json support there is not visible.
Lockfile resolves packages/stack to evlog 1.9.0 (was 1.11.0) and @byteslice/result 0.2.0 (was 0.2.2), adds @cipherstash/auth 0.34.2 with six per-platform optional binaries.
Library logger imports createRequestLogger and initLogger from evlog.
The stash bin is a separate ESM tsup build with a createRequire banner; dependencies other than dotenv/@clack/prompts are left external.
turbo test depends on ^build (dependencies' builds), not the package's own build, so the stash bin is not built for tests.
